257	    private var currentApplies: Applies { Applies(currentPreset) }
258	
259	    /// True while the Size popup's last item, "Custom…", is chosen — which is
260	    /// also the state of a popup whose listing failed, since Custom is then
261	    /// its only item; harmless, because `resolve()` refuses that case before
262	    /// the fields are read.
263	    var isCustomSize: Bool { sizePopup.indexOfSelectedItem == visibleSizes.count }
264	
265	    /// The frame-rate override, or nil for "Project rate" — and always nil
266	    /// for a preset that has no frames, so a rate picked for a movie cannot
267	    /// follow the user into an audio-only export.
268	    private var currentRate: Fps? {
269	        let index = ratePopup.indexOfSelectedItem - 1
270	        guard currentApplies.frameRate, index >= 0, index < Self.rates.count else { return nil }
271	        return Self.rates[index]
272	    }
273	
274	    /// The quality tier, or nil for "Format default" — and, on the same
275	    /// rule, always nil for a preset that takes no bit rate.
276	    private var currentTier: QualityTier? {
277	        let index = qualityPopup.indexOfSelectedItem - 1
278	        guard currentApplies.quality, index >= 0, index < Self.tiers.count else { return nil }
279	        return Self.tiers[index]
280	    }
281	
282	    /// True while the Loudness popup's last item, "Custom…", is chosen.
283	    var isCustomLoudness: Bool {
284	        loudnessPopup.indexOfSelectedItem == Self.loudnessTargets.count + 1
285	    }
286	
287	    /// The integrated target to normalise to, or nil for "Off" — index 0 of
288	    /// the popup, on the Quality row's established rule that the first item
289	    /// is no override at all. Nil too for a format with no sound, so a target
290	    /// picked for a movie cannot follow the user into a GIF.
291	    private var currentLoudness: Double? {
292	        guard currentApplies.loudness else { return nil }
293	        let index = loudnessPopup.indexOfSelectedItem
294	        if index >= 1, index <= Self.loudnessTargets.count {
295	            return Self.loudnessTargets[index - 1]
296	        }
297	        guard isCustomLoudness, !loudnessField.stringValue.isEmpty else { return nil }
298	        let value = loudnessField.doubleValue
299	        guard value.isFinite else { return nil }
300	        return min(
301	            max(value, Self.loudnessRange.lowerBound), Self.loudnessRange.upperBound)
302	    }
303	
304	    /// The size override, or nil when the Size popup is on its first row.
305	    ///
306	    /// That row is the format's default — the first of the core's list and
307	    /// of `visibleSizes` alike, since nothing precedes it to hide it — and
308	    /// it is sent as NO override rather than as its own numbers so that
309	    /// what ⌘E exports and what the `export` tool exports with no `size`
310	    /// are one code path in the core — the default lives in
311	    /// `export_size.rs`, not in two readings of it. Any other row sends
312	    /// that row's numbers; "Custom…" sends the fields', clamped. Nil too
313	    /// for a format that has no frames, so a size picked for a movie cannot
314	    /// follow the user into an audio-only export.
315	    private func sizeOverride() -> (width: Int, height: Int)? {
316	        guard currentApplies.size else { return nil }
317	        if isCustomSize {
318	            return (clampedSize(widthField), clampedSize(heightField))
319	        }
320	        let index = sizePopup.indexOfSelectedItem
321	        guard index > 0, index < visibleSizes.count else { return nil }
322	        return (visibleSizes[index].width, visibleSizes[index].height)
323	    }
324	
325	    /// The frame the controls are ASKING for: the same numbers `overrides()`
326	    /// sends, plus the fallbacks the core would apply to them.
327	    ///
328	    /// The tiers are computed against this rather than against `resolved`,
329	    /// which still describes the PREVIOUS format at the moment a new one is
330	    /// being resolved — the bit rate would then be one change behind the
331	    /// size it was supposed to be for.
332	    private func requestedFormat() -> (width: Int, height: Int, fps: Fps) {
333	        let canvas = editor?.document?.project.snapshot.canvas ?? CanvasSnapshot()
334	        // No override resolves to the Size popup's first row. The format's
335	        // own cap, then the canvas, stand in for it only when the listing
336	        // failed — the same fallback the core applies to a preset with no
337	        // size (`export.rs`).
338	        var width = sizes.first?.width ?? currentPreset?.width ?? canvas.width
339	        var height = sizes.first?.height ?? currentPreset?.height ?? canvas.height
340	        if let size = sizeOverride() {
341	            width = size.width
342	            height = size.height
343	        }
344	        return (width, height, currentRate ?? canvas.fps)
345	    }
346	
347	    /// The override object, with every key the controls are NOT overriding
348	    /// left out — the same rule the op builders follow, so the core's own
349	    /// defaults apply (§6). Keys are the core's override names in
350	    /// `export.rs` — `width`, `height`, `fps`, `range`, `video_bitrate`,
351	    /// `audio_bitrate`.
352	    private func overrides() -> [String: Any]? {
353	        var overrides: [String: Any] = [:]
354	        let applies = currentApplies
355	        let format = requestedFormat()
356	        if let size = sizeOverride() {
357	            overrides["width"] = size.width
358	            overrides["height"] = size.height
359	        }
360	        if let fps = currentRate {
361	            overrides["fps"] = [fps.num, fps.den]
362	        }
363	        // Bits per second: the unit `export.rs` reads these two overrides in,
364	        // and the one `AVVideoAverageBitRateKey` takes after it. They are
365	        // sent separately because a preset may take one and not the other —
366	        // the audio-only row has no video rate to set, and a frame-sequence
367	        // row has neither.
368	        if let tier = currentTier {
369	            if applies.videoBitrate {
370	                overrides["video_bitrate"] = tier.videoBitsPerSecond(
371	                    width: format.width, height: format.height, fps: format.fps,
372	                    codec: currentPreset?.codec ?? "")
373	            }
374	            if applies.audioBitrate {
375	                overrides["audio_bitrate"] = tier.audioBitsPerSecond
376	            }
377	        }
378	        // Both loudness keys together: the ceiling, fixed at −1 dBTP and
379	        // named in the hint, is the master limiter's (spec §11 AU-27), which
380	        // holds −1 unsent too, so a ceiling goes only beside a target.
381	        if let target = currentLoudness {
382	            overrides["loudness_lufs"] = target
383	            overrides["peak_dbtp"] = Self.peakCeilingDBTP
384	        }
385	        // The core reads the range as ONE nested object (`export.rs`), and
386	        // ignores override keys it does not know — so `start` and `duration`
387	        // spelled at the top level exported the whole project instead of the
388	        // in/out range, silently.
389	        if let picture = dynamicRangeOverride() { overrides["dynamic_range"] = picture }
390	        if let speed = encoderSpeedOverride() { overrides["encoder_speed"] = speed }
391	        if let bits = audioBitsOverride() { overrides["audio_bits"] = bits }
392	        if let stems = stemsOverride() { overrides["stems"] = stems }
393	        if rangePopup.indexOfSelectedItem == 1, let range = range {
394	            overrides["range"] = [
395	                "start": range.start,
396	                "duration": max(0, range.end - range.start),
397	            ]
398	        }
399	        return overrides.isEmpty ? nil : overrides
400	    }

402	    private func clampedSize(_ field: NSTextField) -> Int {
403	        min(max(field.integerValue, Self.sizeRange.lowerBound), Self.sizeRange.upperBound)
404	    }

406	    /// Rewrites the readout, the footnote, the controls' enablement and the
407	    /// Export button from `resolved`. The size fields follow the core while
408	    /// a row of the Size popup owns the size, which is what makes "Custom…"
409	    /// readable: pick it and the fields already hold the numbers to edit.
410	    ///
411	    /// Enablement comes from the FORMAT rather than from `resolved`, so a
412	    /// refused resolve leaves the controls where they were instead of
413	    /// greying out the very one that has to be changed to fix it.
414	    private func syncReadout() {
415	        let applies = currentApplies
416	        let custom = isCustomSize
417	        // A popup whose listing failed holds nothing to choose, and the one
418	        // control that can put a size back is the Format popup, so the size
419	        // controls grey out with it — the exception to the rule in the doc
420	        // comment above, for the one refusal no size can fix.
421	        let listed = sizesError == nil
422	        sizePopup.isEnabled = applies.size && listed
423	        for field in [widthField, heightField] {
424	            field.isEnabled = applies.size && listed && custom
425	            field.textColor = field.isEnabled ? DS.textStrong : DS.textMuted
426	        }
427	        ratePopup.isEnabled = applies.frameRate
428	        qualityPopup.isEnabled = applies.quality
429	        syncQualityTitles(applies)
430	        loudnessPopup.isEnabled = applies.loudness
431	        loudnessField.isEnabled = applies.loudness && isCustomLoudness
432	        loudnessField.textColor = loudnessField.isEnabled ? DS.textStrong : DS.textMuted
433	        if !isCustomLoudness {
434	            // The field mirrors the row that is chosen, exactly as the size
435	            // fields mirror the core's answer, so picking "Custom…" starts
436	            // from the number that was in force a moment before. "Off" has no
437	            // number of its own, so it shows the first target — the one
438	            // Custom is most likely to be an adjustment of.
439	            loudnessField.doubleValue = currentLoudness ?? Self.loudnessTargets[0]
440	        }
441	        // The last control on the card, and the last one to be gated: the
442	        // burn-in stayed live on the three audio-only rows, alone among the
443	        // format-dependent controls, offering to write a timecode into a file
444	        // with no picture to write it into.
445	        burnInCheckbox.isEnabled = applies.burnIn
446	        syncDynamicRange(applies)
447	        syncSpeed(applies)
448	        syncAudioBits(applies)
449	        syncStems(applies)
450	
451	        guard let settings = resolved else {
452	            summaryLabel.stringValue = resolveError ?? "These settings are not available."
453	            summaryLabel.textColor = DS.textStrong
454	            footnote.stringValue = ""
455	            footnote.toolTip = nil
456	            exportButton?.isEnabled = false
457	            return
458	        }
459	        if !custom {
460	            widthField.integerValue = settings.width
461	            heightField.integerValue = settings.height
462	        }
463	        summaryLabel.textColor = DS.textMuted
464	        summaryLabel.stringValue = summary(for: settings)
465	        footnote.stringValue = footnoteText(for: settings)
466	        footnote.toolTip = footnote.stringValue
467	        exportButton?.isEnabled = settings.duration > 0
468	    }

470	    /// Re-titles the tier rows with the rate each would ask for at the size
471	    /// and frame rate now chosen. "High" on its own says nothing; "High ·
472	    /// 8.0 Mbps" is the control's actual promise, and it has to move when
473	    /// the frame it is a rate for moves.
474	    private func syncQualityTitles(_ applies: Applies) {
475	        let format = requestedFormat()
476	        let codec = currentPreset?.codec ?? ""
477	        for (index, tier) in Self.tiers.enumerated() {
478	            guard let item = qualityPopup.item(at: index + 1) else { continue }
479	            if applies.videoBitrate {
480	                let rate = tier.videoBitsPerSecond(
481	                    width: format.width, height: format.height, fps: format.fps, codec: codec)
482	                let soft = applies.softCap ? "usually ≤ " : ""   // spec §11 CX-13
483	                item.title = "\(tier.name) · \(soft)\(Self.rateText(rate))"
484	            } else if applies.audioBitrate {
485	                item.title = "\(tier.name) · \(Self.rateText(tier.audioBitsPerSecond))"
486	            } else {
487	                item.title = tier.name
488	            }
489	        }
490	    }

492	    /// The one-line description of what the file will contain.
493	    private func summary(for settings: ExportSettings) -> String {
494	        if settings.isAudioOnly {
495	            // Milliseconds rather than frames, and no rate in the line: audio
496	            // has no frames, which is the same reason the rate popup is
497	            // greyed out for this preset.
498	            let duration = ReelTime.format(settings.duration, fps: settings.fps, frames: false)
499	            return "Audio only · \(duration)"
500	        }
501	        let duration = ReelTime.format(settings.duration, fps: settings.fps, frames: true)
502	        var text = "\(settings.width) × \(settings.height) · \(settings.fps.displayName) fps · "
503	            + duration
504	        if Self.isFrameSequence(container: settings.container) {
505	            // What a GIF or an APNG costs is frames, not seconds — and it
506	            // carries no audio however much of it the timeline has, which is
507	            // worth saying before the export rather than after it.
508	            text += " · \(settings.sequenceFrameCount ?? 0) frames, no audio"
509	        }
510	        // A bundled encoder's estimate (spec §11 CX-18 (9)).
511	        if let line = ExportEncoderCosts.sheetLine(for: settings) { text += "\n" + line }
512	        return text
513	    }
514	
515	    /// The footnote over the buttons: the codec, the container, and the rates
516	    /// the CORE resolved — never the ones the tier asked for, and not filtered by
517	    /// what the sheet thinks applies, since a preset is free to carry a rate
518	    /// of its own that no control here offered.
519	    ///
520	    /// The distinction matters because `export.rs` drops override keys it
521	    /// does not know, silently (the same trap the range comment above names).
522	    /// A tier picked against a core that has no bit-rate overrides has to
523	    /// read as "the format's own rate" rather than let the popup imply a
524	    /// number the file will not have.
525	    private func footnoteText(for settings: ExportSettings) -> String {
526	        var parts = [settings.codec.uppercased()]
527	        let container = settings.container.uppercased()
528	        // A frame-sequence preset's codec IS its container: "GIF · GIF".
529	        if container != parts[0] { parts.append(container) }
530	        if let speed = settings.encoderSpeed { parts.append(speed.menuName) }
531	        if settings.audioBits == 24 { parts.append("24-bit") }
532	        if case let n = settings.stems.count, n > 0 { parts.append(n == 1 ? "1 stem" : "\(n) stems") }
533	        if let rate = settings.videoBitrate {
534	            // A bundled encoder's rate is a soft cap (spec §11 CX-13).
535	            parts.append((settings.writer == nil ? "" : "usually ≤ ") + Self.rateText(rate))
536	        }
537	        if let rate = settings.audioBitrate {
538	            parts.append("\(Self.rateText(rate)) audio")
539	        }
540	        if currentTier != nil, settings.videoBitrate == nil, settings.audioBitrate == nil {
541	            parts.append("format's own rate")
542	        }
543	        // The core's echo, not the popup's row: a build whose
544	        // `export_settings` has never heard of `loudness_lufs` drops the key
545	        // silently, and the footnote must not then promise a normalisation
546	        // the file will not have.
547	        if let target = settings.loudnessLufs {
548	            parts.append(
549	                String(format: "%g LUFS", target).replacingOccurrences(of: "-", with: "−"))
550	        }
551	        // Whether the ENCODING carries a fourth channel — the core's own
552	        // answer for this row (`ExportSettings.alpha`), never a reading of the
553	        // canvas. It is the one place the sheet says which format keeps a
554	        // transparent background, and it is a POSITIVE claim only: the rows
555	        // that answer false are not enumerated here, because the flag says
556	        // what the settings object says and the footnote's whole rule is that
557	        // it reports the core rather than the popup.
558	        if settings.alpha { parts.append("alpha") }
559	        return parts.joined(separator: " · ")
560	    }
561	}

566	    /// Whether the picked format can take a burn-in.
567	    ///
568	    /// It was the one FORMAT-DEPENDENT control on the card that `Applies` did
569	    /// not answer for, and it stayed live on the three audio-only rows while
570	    /// Size, Frame rate and Quality greyed out around it — a checkbox
571	    /// promising to write a timecode into a file with no picture. The tick was
572	    /// inert on the FILE (`ExporterWriter.addVideo` returns at
573	    /// `settings.isAudioOnly`, so an audio-only export composes no frame at
574	    /// all), which is why nothing downstream ever complained; what it was not

536	/// What the export sheet's controls MEAN, before any of them has been read:
537	/// the ranges the fields accept, the loudness targets and the fixed ceiling,
538	/// the quality ladder and its arithmetic, and `Applies` — the one reading of
539	/// a format that decides which of the sheet's controls that row can honestly
540	/// take.
541	///
542	/// The seam is between a control's VOCABULARY and its VALUE.
543	/// `ExportSheetController.swift` builds the popups and the fields and puts
544	/// the card up; `ExportSheetResolve.swift` reads what is chosen and asks the
545	/// core about it. Everything here is what both of them consult and neither
546	/// of them owns: it depends on no popup's selection, holds no state, and
547	/// would answer the same for a sheet that was never shown. That is also why
548	/// the two nested types live in this half rather than beside the controls
549	/// they gate — `QualityTier` is a bit-rate calculation and `Applies` is a
550	/// reading of one `ExportPreset` row, and neither has ever asked an
551	/// `NSPopUpButton` a question.
552	///
553	/// The cut is the size payment `ExportSheetController.swift` owed at 1114
554	/// lines against app/CLAUDE.md's ~600 cap, and it is a pure move: the same
555	/// declarations, in the same order, with the same bodies. **The toll is
556	/// visibility.** `private` on an extension member reaches only its own file,
557	/// so `loudnessTargets`, `loudnessRange`, `tiers`, `QualityTier`, `Applies`,
558	/// `isFrameSequence` and `rateText` are all internal now, for the reason
559	/// `ExporterLoudness.swift` records: the split, and nothing else. `sizeRange`
560	/// and `peakCeilingDBTP` were already internal and say in their own comments
561	/// why. `loudnessTitle` arrived later, in phase 7, and for the other reason a
562	/// member moves: the controller was at the cap and had to give something up
563	/// before it took the Preset row on.
564	extension ExportSheetController {
565	
566	    /// The widest and narrowest custom size the fields accept. Not a format
567	    /// limit: a sanity range so a mistyped digit cannot ask the encoder for a
568	    /// 300 000-pixel frame.
569	    /// Internal, not private: the agent's `export` refuses a custom size
570	    /// outside it by name (`AgentServer+Export.swift`), and one constant is
571	    /// how the sheet and the tool cannot disagree.
572	    static let sizeRange = 16...8192
573	
574	    // MARK: - Loudness
575	
576	    /// The Loudness popup's rows after "Off", in menu order: the integrated
577	    /// target each asks the export to be normalised to.
578	    ///
579	    /// −14 LUFS is where every streaming service has settled (Spotify,
580	    /// YouTube and Apple Music all normalise to within a decibel of it), −16
581	    /// is the podcast convention for stereo, and −23 is EBU R 128, which is
582	    /// broadcast delivery in Europe and what "LUFS" meant before streaming
583	    /// took the word. Anything else is "Custom…" and the field beside it.
584	    static let loudnessTargets: [Double] = [-14, -16, -23]
585	
586	    /// The true-peak ceiling of the master limiter every export with sound
587	    /// runs (spec §11 AU-27), in dBTP, sent only beside a loudness target —
588	    /// unsent, the master holds the same −1 (`ExportLoudness.defaultCeiling`).
589	    /// FIXED in phase 5 rather than made a control: five presets and
590	    /// one broadcast-standard ceiling is what people actually pick, the sheet
591	    /// is already six control rows deep, and the `export` tool keeps
592	    /// `peak_dbtp` for a script that needs −0.3 or −2.0. The hint says the
593	    /// number, so a fixed value is visible rather than folklore.
594	    static let peakCeilingDBTP: Double = -1
595	
596	    /// A target as its menu row reads. The two named tiers say who asks for
597	    /// them, because "−14" and "−23" mean nothing to someone who has not met
598	    /// them before and everything to someone who has.
599	    ///
600	    /// Here rather than beside the popup it titles, and the move is the size
601	    /// payment `ExportSheetController.swift` owed before phase 7 put a Preset
602	    /// row and a burn-in on it. It belongs in this half by this file's own
603	    /// rule: it is a pure function of a target, holds no state, asks no
604	    /// control anything, and is `rateText`'s sibling — the spelling of one of
605	    /// the ladders `loudnessTargets` and `tiers` declare a few lines up.
606	    static func loudnessTitle(_ target: Double) -> String {
607	        let value = String(format: "%.0f", target).replacingOccurrences(of: "-", with: "−")
608	        switch target {
609	        case -14: return "\(value) LUFS (streaming)"
610	        case -23: return "\(value) LUFS (broadcast)"
611	        default: return "\(value) LUFS"
612	        }
613	    }
614	
615	    /// What the core will take: `export_overrides.rs`'s own bounds for
616	    /// `loudness_lufs`, spelled here so the field's formatter refuses what
617	    /// the core would refuse rather than sending it and reading the message
618	    /// back.
619	    static let loudnessRange: ClosedRange<Double> = -70...0
620	
621	    // MARK: - Quality
622	
623	    /// One row of the Quality popup: a video rate expressed as bits per pixel
624	    /// per frame, and the AAC rate that goes with it.
625	    ///
626	    /// **Where the video numbers come from.** They are anchored on one
627	    /// published figure and scaled from it rather than guessed: YouTube's
628	    /// recommended upload for 1080p SDR H.264 at 30 fps is 8 Mbps, and
629	    /// 1920 × 1080 × 30 is 62.2 Mpixel/s, so "High" is 8 000 000 / 62 200 000
630	    /// ≈ 0.129 bits per pixel per frame. The other three tiers are 0.5×,
631	    /// 0.75× and 1.5× of it — 4, 6 and 12 Mbps at 1080p30, which brackets
632	    /// Apple's HLS Authoring Specification 1080p H.264 rung (6.0–7.8 Mbps)
633	    /// on both sides.
634	    ///
635	    /// Holding bits-per-pixel constant makes the rate scale with the frame's
636	    /// area, so High is 3.6 Mbps at 720p and 32 Mbps at 4K. That is
637	    /// deliberately flatter than YouTube's own ladder, which is generous at
638	    /// the small end because its rungs are transcode targets; a master at a
639	    /// constant bits-per-pixel is the same picture at every size, which is
640	    /// what choosing "High" ought to mean.
641	    struct QualityTier {
642	        let name: String
643	        /// Bits per pixel per frame, for H.264 at 30 fps or less.
644	        let bitsPerPixel: Double
645	        /// AAC-LC stereo, bits per second. 128 kbps is the streaming
646	        /// baseline, 256 is what Apple Music ships, and 320 is where AAC-LC
647	        /// stops paying for the extra bits.
648	        let audioBitsPerSecond: Int
649	
650	        /// The video rate for a `width` × `height` frame at `fps`.
651	        ///
652	        /// The 30 is not a stand-in for `fps`: the frame rate enters through
653	        /// `rateFactor` instead, because bits do not scale linearly with it.
654	        /// Consecutive frames are more alike the closer together they are,
655	        /// which is why YouTube's ladder asks 1.5× for its 48–60 fps column
656	        /// and nothing extra for 24 fps over 30. This mirrors that shape —
657	        /// one step at 30 and below, one above it.
658	        func videoBitsPerSecond(width: Int, height: Int, fps: Fps, codec: String) -> Int {
659	            let pixels = Double(max(width, 1)) * Double(max(height, 1))
660	            let rateFactor = fps.double > 30.5 ? 1.5 : 1.0
661	            // HEVC reaches the same picture at roughly 60 % of H.264's rate —
662	            // the ratio between the two 1080p rungs of the same Apple
663	            // specification the tiers are calibrated against. AV1 takes
664	            // HEVC's factor (spec §11 CX-9 (2)): its efficiency goes to the
665	            // picture, not the file size. VP9 takes it too (CX-9 (2), CX-16 (7)).
666	            let lower = codec.lowercased()
667	            let codecFactor = QualityTier.isHEVC(codec) || lower == "av1" || lower == "vp9"
668	                ? 0.6 : 1.0
669	            let bits = pixels * 30 * bitsPerPixel * rateFactor * codecFactor
670	            // To the nearest 100 kbps: these are estimates, and a request for
671	            // "7 963 200 bits" would claim a precision they do not have.
672	            return max(100_000, Int((bits / 100_000).rounded()) * 100_000)
673	        }
674	
675	        private static func isHEVC(_ codec: String) -> Bool {
676	            let codec = codec.lowercased()
677	            return codec.hasPrefix("hevc") || codec.hasPrefix("h265") || codec.hasPrefix("h.265")
678	        }
679	    }
680	
681	    /// The tiers, in menu order. Index 0 of the popup is "Format default",
682	    /// i.e. no override at all — the format's own rate, or the export
683	    /// session's ladder when it carries none.
684	    static let tiers: [QualityTier] = [
685	        QualityTier(name: "Low", bitsPerPixel: 0.064, audioBitsPerSecond: 128_000),
686	        QualityTier(name: "Medium", bitsPerPixel: 0.096, audioBitsPerSecond: 192_000),
687	        QualityTier(name: "High", bitsPerPixel: 0.129, audioBitsPerSecond: 256_000),
688	        QualityTier(name: "Maximum", bitsPerPixel: 0.193, audioBitsPerSecond: 320_000),
689	    ]
690	
691	    /// What the picked format can actually take from this sheet.
692	    ///
693	    /// Both the enablement of every control AND every override key are read
694	    /// from one of these, so a greyed-out control can never still be sending
695	    /// a value to the core — which is what keeps the sheet honest as formats
696	    /// that are not H.264 movies join the list.
697	    struct Applies {
698	        private let preset: ExportPreset?
699	
700	        init(_ preset: ExportPreset?) {
701	            self.preset = preset
702	        }
703	
704	        /// A frame sequence — GIF or APNG — has a size and a frame rate but
705	        /// no bit rate to spend and no audio track to put one on.
706	        private var frameSequence: Bool {
707	            guard let preset = preset else { return false }
708	            return ExportSheetController.isFrameSequence(container: preset.container)
709	        }
710	
711	        /// A row whose data rate is not the sheet's to name. ProRes is a
712	        /// fixed-rate intra codec — the profile decides — and §7.8's preset
713	        /// pairs it with LPCM audio; the two LPCM audio rows are
714	        /// uncompressed by definition, so offering either of them an AAC bit
715	        /// rate would be a control that changes nothing about the file. Both
716	        /// are `ExportSettings.carriesLinearPCM(codec:)`.
717	        private var fixedRate: Bool {
718	            ExportSettings.carriesLinearPCM(codec: preset?.codec ?? "")
719	        }
720	
721	        private var hasVideo: Bool { preset.map { !$0.audioOnly } ?? false }
722	
723	        var size: Bool { hasVideo }
724	        var frameRate: Bool { hasVideo }
725	        var videoBitrate: Bool { hasVideo && !frameSequence && !fixedRate }
726	        var audioBitrate: Bool { preset != nil && !frameSequence && !fixedRate }
727	        var quality: Bool { videoBitrate || audioBitrate }
728	
729	        /// Loudness normalisation is a gain on the mixed sound, so it
730	        /// applies to every row that HAS sound — which is every row but the
731	        /// two frame sequences. Deliberately not gated by `fixedRate` (ProRes
732	        /// carries LPCM audio and takes a gain like anything else) nor by
733	        /// `hasVideo` (the three audio-only rows are exactly where a
734	        /// delivery target matters most).
735	        var loudness: Bool { preset != nil && !frameSequence }
736	
737	        /// The Dynamic Range popup is live only on a row that carries an HLG
738	        /// project's HDR picture (spec §11 HD-14 (h)).
739	        var dynamicRange: Bool { preset?.carriesHDR ?? false }
740	
741	        /// The Speed popup is live only on a row whose bundled encoder has
742	        /// speeds (spec §11 CX-12 (2); not `vp9_webm`, CX-16 (2)).
743	        var encoderSpeed: Bool { !(preset?.encoderSpeeds.isEmpty ?? true) }
744	
745	        /// The Bit depth popup is live only on a row that lists depths: the
746	        /// uncompressed WAV and AIFF rows (spec §11 AU-29).
747	        var audioBits: Bool { !(preset?.audioBits.isEmpty ?? true) }
748	
749	        /// The Stems popup is live only on a row that lists modes: the three
750	        /// audio rows (spec §11 AU-108 (a)).
751	        var stems: Bool { !(preset?.stems.isEmpty ?? true) }
752	
753	        /// The video rate is a soft cap on every row a bundled encoder writes
754	        /// (spec §11 CX-13, CX-16 (7)), whether or not it has speeds.
755	        var softCap: Bool { preset?.writer != nil }
756	    }
757	
758	    /// GIF and APNG. Spelled once, and taken from the container rather than
759	    /// the codec because that is the field both `ExportPreset` and
760	    /// `ExportSettings` carry.
761	    static func isFrameSequence(container: String) -> Bool {
762	        let container = container.lowercased()
763	        return container == "gif" || container == "apng"
764	    }
765	
766	    /// A bit rate as the tier rows and the footnote spell it.
767	    static func rateText(_ bitsPerSecond: Int) -> String {
768	        if bitsPerSecond >= 1_000_000 {
769	            return String(format: "%.1f Mbps", Double(bitsPerSecond) / 1_000_000)
770	        }
771	        return "\(Int((Double(bitsPerSecond) / 1000).rounded())) kbps"
772	    }

779	/// reach it, `recipeOptions`, `suggestedName` and `panelMessage`. An extension of
780	/// `ExportSheetController` in a file of its own, a pure move out of the controller before the
781	/// HDR road map's export range (hdr H-0).
782	extension ExportSheetController {
783	    // MARK: - Commit
784	
785	    @objc func cancelClicked(_ sender: Any?) {
786	        dismiss(self)
787	    }
788	
789	    /// Export… — write it now, behind a progress sheet.
790	    @objc func exportClicked(_ sender: Any?) {
791	        commit(queue: false)
792	    }
793	
794	    /// Add to Queue — write it later, behind nothing. The SAME commit, in one
795	    /// method, so the buttons cannot drift (road map 2's phase 7e).
796	    @objc func queueClicked(_ sender: Any?) {
797	        commit(queue: true)
798	    }
799	
800	    /// Hands off to the save panel, then to `EditorViewController`'s
801	    /// `beginExport` — or, for Add to Queue, its `enqueueExport`. The settings
802	    /// are captured BEFORE the dismissal: after it this controller's window is
803	    /// gone and its controls are on their way out of the view tree. Everything
804	    /// above the handoff is the same for both buttons and is written once for
805	    /// that reason: a queued job is not a second kind of export, it is this
806	    /// one held until its turn.
807	    private func commit(queue: Bool) {
808	        // End any edit in a Custom field first. A mouse click on a button
809	        // does not take the first responder from a text field, so the value
810	        // typed there has not been committed — `controlTextDidEndEditing`,
811	        // and the resolve it runs, fire only when the field editor resigns —
812	        // and `resolved` still describes the size from BEFORE the edit.
813	        // Handing the first responder to nobody makes it resign now,
814	        // synchronously, so the read below sees the numbers on screen. A
815	        // field whose text its formatter rejects refuses to resign; that is
816	        // the person's to fix, so the click just beeps.
817	        guard endSheetFieldEditing() else { return }
818	        guard let editor = editor, let settings = resolved,
819	              let window = editor.view.window
820	        else {
821	            NSSound.beep()
822	            return
823	        }
824	        // Read while the controls still exist. `recipeOptions` is not part of
825	        // `settings` and never can be: the burn-in changes the PICTURE, so it
826	        // travels with the description of the picture rather than through the
827	        // override table, which drops a key it does not know without a word
828	        // (`RecipeOptions`).
829	        let options = recipeOptions
830	        // Remembered on the COMMIT and not on the dismissal: a card somebody
831	        // opened, fiddled with and cancelled is not a choice they made — and
832	        // queueing a job is as much a choice as exporting one, so both
833	        // buttons record it.
834	        currentChoice.remember()
835	        let name = suggestedName(for: settings, in: editor)
836	        dismiss(self)
837	
838	        let panel = NSSavePanel()
839	        panel.nameFieldStringValue = name
840	        panel.canCreateDirectories = true
841	        panel.isExtensionHidden = false
842	        panel.message = Self.panelMessage(for: settings)
843	        if let type = Exporter.contentType(for: settings) {
844	            panel.allowedContentTypes = [type]
845	        }
846	        // AppKit queues this behind the sheet that is on its way out, so the
847	        // panel appears once the settings card has finished leaving.
848	        panel.beginSheetModal(for: window) { [weak editor] response in
849	            guard response == .OK, let url = panel.url, let editor = editor else { return }
850	            // The handoff, and the only place the two buttons differ. The
851	            // project and its media are read on the far side of it, at the
852	            // moment the destination is known — which for a queued job is the
853	            // whole of what makes it immutable (`ExportQueueController`).
854	            if queue {
855	                editor.enqueueExport(settings: settings, to: url, options: options)
856	            } else {
857	                editor.beginExport(settings: settings, to: url, options: options)
858	            }
859	        }
860	    }
861	
862	    /// What the card asks of the RECIPE rather than of the export settings —
863	    /// today, the burn-in and nothing else.
864	    var recipeOptions: RecipeOptions {
865	        RecipeOptions(burnInTimecode: burnInCheckbox.state == .on)
866	    }
867	
868	    /// The document's name with the container's extension: `displayStem`, the
869	    /// title with the package's own extension off and NOTHING else off, so
870	    /// "Board v1.2" is `Board v1.2.mp4` (`ProjectDocument+DisplayStem.swift`).
871	    private func suggestedName(for settings: ExportSettings, in editor: EditorViewController)
872	        -> String
873	    {
874	        let stem = editor.document?.displayStem ?? ProjectDocument.untitledDisplayName
875	        return stem + "." + Exporter.fileExtension(for: settings)
876	    }
877	
878	    /// The save panel's one line about what is being written. "As a movie"
879	    /// was wrong for half the table: a GIF or an APNG is an animated image
880	    /// and the audio-only row writes no picture at all. The classes are the
881	    /// sheet's own (`Applies`, `isFrameSequence`), so a format that is
882	    /// neither is a movie by the same reading that gave it a Size popup.
883	    private static func panelMessage(for settings: ExportSettings) -> String {
884	        if settings.isAudioOnly { return "Export the timeline's audio." }
885	        if isFrameSequence(container: settings.container) {
886	            return "Export the timeline as an animated \(settings.container.uppercased())."
887	        }
888	        return "Export the timeline as a movie."
889	    }
890	}

3	/// The export sheet's ANSWER half: read the controls, ask the core what they
4	/// describe, and repaint the card from what it said.
5	///
6	/// The seam is the §7 rule the sheet is built on, drawn as a file boundary.
7	/// `ExportSheetController.swift` owns the controls — it makes the popups and
8	/// the fields, lists the sizes, and hands a person something to choose with.
9	/// Nothing there decides an output size, a rate or a duration, because
10	/// nothing in this dialog does: every number the card shows comes back from
11	/// `rc_export_settings`, and this file is the whole of the round trip. It
12	/// turns a selection into the override object the core reads (`overrides()`),
13	/// sends it (`resolve()`), and writes the answer into the readout, the
14	/// footnote and the controls' enablement (`syncReadout()`). Between those
15	/// three, the `current…` accessors are the one place a popup index becomes a
16	/// meaning, so a control's index arithmetic is never spelled twice.
17	///
18	/// The one number the sheet DOES choose is the bit rate, and it is here for
19	/// that reason rather than beside the Quality popup: a tier is a REQUEST
20	/// (`ExportSheetOptions.swift` holds the ladder), and turning one into bits
21	/// per second needs the frame the controls are asking for — which is
22	/// `requestedFormat()`, three accessors deep into this file and nowhere near
23	/// the popup.
24	///
25	/// The cut is the size payment `ExportSheetController.swift` owed at 1114
26	/// lines against app/CLAUDE.md's ~600 cap, and it is a pure move: the same
27	/// methods, in the same order, with the same bodies. **The toll is
28	/// visibility**, for the reason `ExporterLoudness.swift` records — `private`
29	/// on an extension member reaches only its own file, and a stored property
30	/// cannot live in an extension at all. So every control, every field and
31	/// every piece of state this file reads is internal in the file that
32	/// declares it, and the four members the controls call back into —
33	/// `resolve()`, `currentPreset`, `isCustomSize` and `isCustomLoudness` — are
34	/// internal here. Everything else below stays `private`, because a `private`
35	/// extension member is reachable from the rest of THIS file, and nothing
36	/// outside it has ever asked.
37	/// Phase 7 added the OTHER direction to this file, and it belongs here for the
38	/// same reason the first one does: `currentChoice` is a reading of the
39	/// controls, exactly as `overrides()` is, and `apply(_:)` is that reading run
40	/// backwards. Keeping the pair together is what makes a saved preset and the
41	/// remembered choice provably the same thing as clicking each control by hand —
42	/// there is one account of what a stored choice means, and both halves of it
43	/// are on one screen.
44	extension ExportSheetController {
45	
46	    // MARK: - Resolving
47	
48	    /// Asks the core for the settings the current controls describe, then
49	    /// repaints the readout from the answer.
50	    ///
51	    /// A refusal is not an error dialog: the message goes in the readout and
52	    /// Export greys out, so a bad override reads as "this combination is not
53	    /// available" rather than interrupting the person adjusting it.
54	    func resolve() {
55	        guard let project = editor?.document?.project, let preset = currentPreset else {
56	            resolved = nil
57	            resolveError = "This build has no export presets."
58	            syncReadout()
59	            return
60	        }
61	        // A format whose sizes the core could not list is not exported at
62	        // all, whatever the settings call would answer: the one refusal
63	        // `rc_export_sizes` shares with `rc_export_settings` is an unknown
64	        // preset, but a listing can also fail on its own (a reply this
65	        // build cannot decode), and the size the sheet would then send is
66	        // the fields' clamped floor, 16 × 16, which nobody asked for.
67	        if let message = sizesError {
68	            resolved = nil
69	            resolveError = message
70	            syncReadout()
71	            return
72	        }
73	        // An empty Custom field is not a size. Its formatter accepts the
74	        // empty string as "no value", `integerValue` reads that as 0, and
75	        // the clamp would turn it into the 16-pixel floor — an export
76	        // nobody asked for, reached by clearing a field and clicking
77	        // Export…, since that click commits the field before it reads.
78	        if isCustomSize, currentApplies.size,
79	            widthField.stringValue.isEmpty || heightField.stringValue.isEmpty
80	        {
81	            resolved = nil
82	            resolveError = "Type a width and a height, or pick a size from the list."
83	            syncReadout()
84	            return
85	        }
86	        // The same rule for the Custom loudness field, and for the same
87	        // reason: an empty field is not a target, and reading it as one would
88	        // export at whatever the clamp's floor happens to be.
89	        if isCustomLoudness, currentApplies.loudness, loudnessField.stringValue.isEmpty {
90	            resolved = nil
91	            resolveError = "Type a loudness target in LUFS, or pick one from the list."
92	            syncReadout()
93	            return
94	        }
95	        do {
96	            resolved = try ReelExport.settings(
97	                project, preset: preset.id, overrides: overrides())
98	            resolveError = nil
99	        } catch {
100	            resolved = nil
101	            resolveError = error.localizedDescription
102	        }
103	        syncReadout()
104	    }
105	
106	    // MARK: - The card as a value
107	
108	    /// The controls as an `ExportChoice`, with the sheet's own gating applied:
109	    /// a control the chosen format cannot take (`Applies`) contributes
110	    /// nothing, exactly as it contributes no override. So a preset saved off
111	    /// an audio-only row carries no size, and one saved off a GIF carries no
112	    /// loudness — the record says what was actually asked for and never what
113	    /// a greyed-out popup happened to be sitting on.
114	    ///
115	    /// **The burn-in is gated by that same rule and used not to be**, which
116	    /// broke the sentence above rather than any of the core's: a tick made on
117	    /// an H.264 row and carried across to WAV was written into the record
118	    /// beside a size, an fps and a tier all three deliberately left empty, so
119	    /// a named preset — and the remembered choice, which is this same
120	    /// value — said a file with no picture would carry a burn-in. It is not an
121	    /// override, so nothing downstream ever refused it; `Applies.burnIn`
122	    /// (below) is where it is refused now.
123	    ///
124	    /// The `name` is empty: naming a choice is the Save… item's business.
125	    var currentChoice: ExportChoice {
126	        var choice = ExportChoice(presetID: currentPreset?.id ?? "")
127	        if currentApplies.size {
128	            if isCustomSize {
129	                choice.customSize = [clampedSize(widthField), clampedSize(heightField)]
130	            } else {
131	                let index = sizePopup.indexOfSelectedItem
132	                // The ROW's id, never its index (`ExportChoice.sizeRow`).
133	                // Index 0 is recorded like any other: it is a row a person
134	                // chose, and `sizeOverride()`'s decision to send it as no
135	                // override at all is about the CORE's default and not about
136	                // what the popup was showing.
137	                if index >= 0, index < visibleSizes.count {
138	                    choice.sizeRow = visibleSizes[index].id
139	                }
140	            }
141	        }
142	        choice.fps = currentRate.map { [$0.num, $0.den] }
143	        choice.qualityTier = currentTier?.name
144	        choice.loudness = currentLoudness
145	        choice.inOutRange = rangePopup.indexOfSelectedItem == 1
146	        choice.burnInTimecode = currentApplies.burnIn && recipeOptions.burnInTimecode
147	        choice.encoderSpeed = encoderSpeedChoice.rawValue
148	        choice.audioBits = audioBitsChoice
149	        choice.stems = stemsChoice
150	        return choice
151	    }
152	
153	    /// Writes a stored choice back into the controls. **The order is
154	    /// load-bearing and this method is where it is written down**; every
155	    /// caller — the remembered choice in `loadView`, a preset picked from the
156	    /// popup — goes through here so there is only ever one order.
157	    ///
158	    /// 1. **Format FIRST, before the sizes are listed.** A programmatic
159	    ///    `selectItem` sends no action, so `formatChanged`'s `sizesPreset`
160	    ///    guard never fires and nothing rebuilds on its own; listing after the
161	    ///    pick is what makes the rows this format's rows.
162	    /// 2. **Size AFTER `rebuildSizes()`**, which ends with an unconditional
163	    ///    `sizePopup.selectItem(at: 0)` and would undo a selection made before
164	    ///    it.
165	    /// 3. **A custom LOUDNESS selects "Custom…" first and fills the field
166	    ///    second**, because `syncReadout` overwrites that field from the popup
167	    ///    whenever the popup is not on Custom — and `resolve()` runs one
168	    ///    `syncReadout` after this returns.
169	    /// 4. **`in_out` degrades to "Whole project"** on a document that has no
170	    ///    range: the popup only carries that row when `range != nil`, so
171	    ///    selecting index 1 would select nothing at all.
172	    ///
173	    /// It does NOT resolve. The caller does, once, after the last control has
174	    /// moved — a resolve per control would be six FFI round trips to paint one
175	    /// card.
176	    func apply(_ choice: ExportChoice) {
177	        if let index = presets.firstIndex(where: { $0.id == choice.presetID }) {
178	            formatPopup.selectItem(at: index)
179	        }
180	        rebuildSizes()
181	        applySize(choice)
182	
183	        if let fps = choice.fps, fps.count == 2,
184	            let index = Self.rates.firstIndex(where: { $0.num == fps[0] && $0.den == fps[1] })
185	        {
186	            ratePopup.selectItem(at: index + 1)
187	        } else {
188	            ratePopup.selectItem(at: 0)
189	        }
190	
191	        if let name = choice.qualityTier,
192	            let index = Self.tiers.firstIndex(where: { $0.name == name })
193	        {
194	            qualityPopup.selectItem(at: index + 1)
195	        } else {
196	            qualityPopup.selectItem(at: 0)
197	        }
198	
199	        applyLoudness(choice)
200	        rangePopup.selectItem(at: choice.inOutRange && range != nil ? 1 : 0)
201	        burnInCheckbox.state = choice.burnInTimecode ? .on : .off
202	        applySpeed(choice)
203	        applyAudioBits(choice)
204	        applyStems(choice)
205	    }
206	
207	    /// Step 2, after the listing. A row whose id this format does not offer —
208	    /// a GIF's cap under H.264, or a row `visibleSizes` hid because an earlier
209	    /// row already has its numbers — falls back to the SAME NUMBERS under
210	    /// whatever row does show them, and only then to the format's default.
211	    /// Hiding is a tidiness of the popup's (`visibleSizes`), so a choice of
212	    /// "1080p" on a 1920 × 1080 document has to land on "Document size" rather
213	    /// than be dropped: it is the same export.
214	    private func applySize(_ choice: ExportChoice) {
215	        if let row = choice.sizeRow {
216	            if let index = visibleSizes.firstIndex(where: { $0.id == row }) {
217	                sizePopup.selectItem(at: index)
218	                return
219	            }
220	            if let hidden = sizes.first(where: { $0.id == row }),
221	                let index = visibleSizes.firstIndex(where: {
222	                    $0.width == hidden.width && $0.height == hidden.height
223	                })
224	            {
225	                sizePopup.selectItem(at: index)
226	                return
227	            }
228	            return
229	        }
230	        guard let custom = choice.customSize, custom.count == 2 else { return }
231	        // "Custom…" is the item after the last visible row.
232	        sizePopup.selectItem(at: visibleSizes.count)
233	        widthField.integerValue = custom[0]
234	        heightField.integerValue = custom[1]
235	    }
236	
237	    /// Step 3: the row first, the field second.
238	    private func applyLoudness(_ choice: ExportChoice) {
239	        guard let target = choice.loudness else {
240	            loudnessPopup.selectItem(at: 0)
241	            return
242	        }
243	        if let index = Self.loudnessTargets.firstIndex(of: target) {
244	            loudnessPopup.selectItem(at: index + 1)
245	            return
246	        }
247	        loudnessPopup.selectItem(at: Self.loudnessTargets.count + 1)
248	        loudnessField.doubleValue = target
249	    }
250	
251	    var currentPreset: ExportPreset? {
252	        let index = formatPopup.indexOfSelectedItem
253	        guard index >= 0, index < presets.count else { return nil }
254	        return presets[index]
255	    }
256	
257	    private var currentApplies: Applies { Applies(currentPreset) }
258	
259	    /// True while the Size popup's last item, "Custom…", is chosen — which is
260	    /// also the state of a popup whose listing failed, since Custom is then
261	    /// its only item; harmless, because `resolve()` refuses that case before
262	    /// the fields are read.
263	    var isCustomSize: Bool { sizePopup.indexOfSelectedItem == visibleSizes.count }
264	
265	    /// The frame-rate override, or nil for "Project rate" — and always nil
266	    /// for a preset that has no frames, so a rate picked for a movie cannot
267	    /// follow the user into an audio-only export.
268	    private var currentRate: Fps? {
269	        let index = ratePopup.indexOfSelectedItem - 1
270	        guard currentApplies.frameRate, index >= 0, index < Self.rates.count else { return nil }
271	        return Self.rates[index]
272	    }
273	
274	    /// The quality tier, or nil for "Format default" — and, on the same
275	    /// rule, always nil for a preset that takes no bit rate.
276	    private var currentTier: QualityTier? {
277	        let index = qualityPopup.indexOfSelectedItem - 1
278	        guard currentApplies.quality, index >= 0, index < Self.tiers.count else { return nil }
279	        return Self.tiers[index]
280	    }
281	
282	    /// True while the Loudness popup's last item, "Custom…", is chosen.
283	    var isCustomLoudness: Bool {
284	        loudnessPopup.indexOfSelectedItem == Self.loudnessTargets.count + 1
285	    }
286	
287	    /// The integrated target to normalise to, or nil for "Off" — index 0 of
288	    /// the popup, on the Quality row's established rule that the first item
289	    /// is no override at all. Nil too for a format with no sound, so a target
290	    /// picked for a movie cannot follow the user into a GIF.
291	    private var currentLoudness: Double? {
292	        guard currentApplies.loudness else { return nil }
293	        let index = loudnessPopup.indexOfSelectedItem
294	        if index >= 1, index <= Self.loudnessTargets.count {
295	            return Self.loudnessTargets[index - 1]
296	        }
297	        guard isCustomLoudness, !loudnessField.stringValue.isEmpty else { return nil }
298	        let value = loudnessField.doubleValue
299	        guard value.isFinite else { return nil }
300	        return min(
301	            max(value, Self.loudnessRange.lowerBound), Self.loudnessRange.upperBound)
302	    }
303	
304	    /// The size override, or nil when the Size popup is on its first row.
305	    ///
306	    /// That row is the format's default — the first of the core's list and
307	    /// of `visibleSizes` alike, since nothing precedes it to hide it — and
308	    /// it is sent as NO override rather than as its own numbers so that
309	    /// what ⌘E exports and what the `export` tool exports with no `size`
310	    /// are one code path in the core — the default lives in
311	    /// `export_size.rs`, not in two readings of it. Any other row sends
312	    /// that row's numbers; "Custom…" sends the fields', clamped. Nil too
313	    /// for a format that has no frames, so a size picked for a movie cannot
314	    /// follow the user into an audio-only export.
315	    private func sizeOverride() -> (width: Int, height: Int)? {
316	        guard currentApplies.size else { return nil }
317	        if isCustomSize {
318	            return (clampedSize(widthField), clampedSize(heightField))
319	        }
320	        let index = sizePopup.indexOfSelectedItem
321	        guard index > 0, index < visibleSizes.count else { return nil }
322	        return (visibleSizes[index].width, visibleSizes[index].height)
323	    }
324	
325	    /// The frame the controls are ASKING for: the same numbers `overrides()`
326	    /// sends, plus the fallbacks the core would apply to them.
327	    ///
328	    /// The tiers are computed against this rather than against `resolved`,
329	    /// which still describes the PREVIOUS format at the moment a new one is
330	    /// being resolved — the bit rate would then be one change behind the
331	    /// size it was supposed to be for.
332	    private func requestedFormat() -> (width: Int, height: Int, fps: Fps) {
333	        let canvas = editor?.document?.project.snapshot.canvas ?? CanvasSnapshot()
334	        // No override resolves to the Size popup's first row. The format's
335	        // own cap, then the canvas, stand in for it only when the listing
336	        // failed — the same fallback the core applies to a preset with no
337	        // size (`export.rs`).
338	        var width = sizes.first?.width ?? currentPreset?.width ?? canvas.width
339	        var height = sizes.first?.height ?? currentPreset?.height ?? canvas.height
340	        if let size = sizeOverride() {
341	            width = size.width
342	            height = size.height
343	        }
344	        return (width, height, currentRate ?? canvas.fps)
345	    }
346	
347	    /// The override object, with every key the controls are NOT overriding
348	    /// left out — the same rule the op builders follow, so the core's own
349	    /// defaults apply (§6). Keys are the core's override names in
350	    /// `export.rs` — `width`, `height`, `fps`, `range`, `video_bitrate`,
351	    /// `audio_bitrate`.
352	    private func overrides() -> [String: Any]? {
353	        var overrides: [String: Any] = [:]
354	        let applies = currentApplies
355	        let format = requestedFormat()
356	        if let size = sizeOverride() {
357	            overrides["width"] = size.width
358	            overrides["height"] = size.height
359	        }
360	        if let fps = currentRate {
361	            overrides["fps"] = [fps.num, fps.den]
362	        }
363	        // Bits per second: the unit `export.rs` reads these two overrides in,
364	        // and the one `AVVideoAverageBitRateKey` takes after it. They are
365	        // sent separately because a preset may take one and not the other —
366	        // the audio-only row has no video rate to set, and a frame-sequence
367	        // row has neither.
368	        if let tier = currentTier {
369	            if applies.videoBitrate {
370	                overrides["video_bitrate"] = tier.videoBitsPerSecond(
371	                    width: format.width, height: format.height, fps: format.fps,
372	                    codec: currentPreset?.codec ?? "")
373	            }
374	            if applies.audioBitrate {
375	                overrides["audio_bitrate"] = tier.audioBitsPerSecond
376	            }
377	        }
378	        // Both loudness keys together: the ceiling, fixed at −1 dBTP and
379	        // named in the hint, is the master limiter's (spec §11 AU-27), which
380	        // holds −1 unsent too, so a ceiling goes only beside a target.
381	        if let target = currentLoudness {
382	            overrides["loudness_lufs"] = target
383	            overrides["peak_dbtp"] = Self.peakCeilingDBTP
384	        }
385	        // The core reads the range as ONE nested object (`export.rs`), and
386	        // ignores override keys it does not know — so `start` and `duration`
387	        // spelled at the top level exported the whole project instead of the
388	        // in/out range, silently.
389	        if let picture = dynamicRangeOverride() { overrides["dynamic_range"] = picture }
390	        if let speed = encoderSpeedOverride() { overrides["encoder_speed"] = speed }
391	        if let bits = audioBitsOverride() { overrides["audio_bits"] = bits }
392	        if let stems = stemsOverride() { overrides["stems"] = stems }
393	        if rangePopup.indexOfSelectedItem == 1, let range = range {
394	            overrides["range"] = [
395	                "start": range.start,
396	                "duration": max(0, range.end - range.start),
397	            ]
398	        }
399	        return overrides.isEmpty ? nil : overrides

input.content:
---
title: "The export sheet"
description: "Choose a format and its settings, see what the file will be before anything is written, then export now or add the job to the queue."
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

One sheet turns the timeline into a movie, an audio file or an animated image. It shows you the size, rate, length and codec of the file before anything is written.

<AtAGlance
  menu="File ▸ Export…"
  keys="⌘E"
  where="The accent Export… button at the right end of the toolbar"
  tools={['export', 'export_status', 'cancel_export']}
/>

## Open the export sheet

<Steps>

1. Choose **File ▸ Export…**, press <kbd>⌘E</kbd>, or click **Export…** at the right end of the toolbar. Playback pauses and the sheet opens over the editor window.

2. Choose a [format](/export/formats/), then change whichever other controls you need.

3. Read the [readout line](#the-readout-line) and the [footnote](#the-footnote) under the controls. They say what the file will be.

4. Choose [**Export…** or **Add to Queue**](#export-or-add-to-queue), then pick where to save the file.

</Steps>

While the timeline is empty, **File ▸ Export…** is greyed out and there's no sheet to open. A timeline of nothing but text, shapes, images and graphics still exports. You can't edit the project while the sheet is open.

An export always writes the whole timeline, even when you're working inside a [nest](/editing/nests/).

<Shot
  name="12-export-sheet.sheet"
  alt="The Export sheet with a paragraph of help under its title, then the controls: Preset on Custom, Format on H.264 (MP4), Speed greyed on Balanced, Size on Document size 960 × 540 with two greyed fields, Frame rate on Project rate, Quality on Format default, Bit depth greyed on 16-bit, Stems greyed on None, Loudness on Off, Range greyed on Whole project, and an unticked Burn in timecode. Below them the readout reads 960 × 540, 30 fps, 00:00:05:07, the footnote reads H264, MP4, and the buttons are Add to Queue, Cancel and Export…."
/>

## The controls

From top to bottom:

| Control | What it does | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Preset:** | Applies a set of choices you saved. The gear beside it saves and deletes them. See [Export presets](/export/presets/). | Custom |
| **Format:** | The encoding, a container and a codec together. See [Choose a format](/export/formats/). | H.264 (MP4) |
| **Dynamic Range:** | Which picture an HDR project writes. The row is there only in an HLG project. See [Export HDR](/hdr/export-hdr/). | HDR (HLG) |
| **Speed:** | How long the AV1 encoder works on each frame. See [Encoder speed](/export/encoder-speed/). | Balanced |
| **Size:** | The frame size, or **Custom…** with width and height fields on the row below. See [Export size](/export/size/). | The format's first row |
| **Frame rate:** | **Project rate**, or a fixed rate. See [Export frame rate](/export/frame-rate/). | Project rate |
| **Quality:** | **Format default**, or a bit-rate tier. See [Export quality](/export/quality/). | Format default |
| **Bit depth:** | **16-bit** or **24-bit**, for a WAV or an AIFF. See [Export bit depth](/export/bit-depth/). | 16-bit |
| **Stems:** | Also writes each track's sound as its own file. See [Audio stems](/export/stems/). | None |
| **Loudness:** | **Off**, a loudness target, or **Custom…** with a LUFS field. See [Export loudness](/export/loudness/). | Off |
| **Range:** | **Whole project**, or **In/out range** when one is set. See [Export a range](/export/range/). | Whole project |
| **Burn in timecode** | Draws the project timecode into the exported picture. See [Burn in timecode](/export/burn-in-timecode/). | Off |

Every export's sound goes through a master limiter, whatever you choose here. See [Export loudness](/export/loudness/).

## Unavailable controls

A control the chosen format can't use is greyed out rather than hidden, and its value isn't sent. So a greyed-out control never affects the file.

| Control | Available on |
| --- | --- |
| **Dynamic Range:** | HEVC 10-bit (MP4), AV1 (MP4), AV1 (WebM), VP9 (WebM), ProRes 422 (MOV) and ProRes 4444 (MOV). On any other format it's greyed out and shows **SDR version**, which is what that format writes. |
| **Speed:** | AV1 (MP4) and AV1 (WebM) |
| **Size:**, **Frame rate:** and **Burn in timecode** | Every format but the three audio-only ones |
| **Quality:** | Every format but ProRes, WAV, AIFF, GIF and APNG |
| **Bit depth:** | Audio only (WAV) and Audio only (AIFF) |
| **Stems:** | The three audio-only formats |
| **Loudness:** | Every format but GIF and APNG |

**Speed:**, **Bit depth:** and **Stems:** go on showing your last choice while they're greyed out, and it comes back when you pick a format that uses it.

**Range:** doesn't depend on the format. It's greyed out when the project has no in/out range. It's greyed out inside a nest too, even when the nest has a range, and its tooltip says why: an export writes the whole timeline, so it can't use a range that belongs to the nest. Leave the nest with <kbd>⌘↑</kbd> and set a range on the timeline.

## The readout line

The line under the controls says what size, rate and length the file will have. These are the file's real numbers, so a GIF's fitted size or an evened edge shows here.

| Kind of file | The readout looks like |
| --- | --- |
| A movie | `1920 × 1080 · 30 fps · 00:01:12:05` |
| An audio-only file | `Audio only · 00:01:12.200` |
| A GIF or APNG | The movie line, followed by `· 360 frames, no audio` |

When the sheet can't work out a valid file, the readout says what to fix and **Export…** and **Add to Queue** are greyed out. An empty custom field gives "Type a width and a height, or pick a size from the list." or "Type a loudness target in LUFS, or pick one from the list."

## Estimated time

On AV1 (MP4), AV1 (WebM), VP9 (WebM) and VP9 with Alpha (WebM) a second line estimates how long the export will take, for example `Estimated time: about 25 s`. The other formats show no estimate.

| How long | It reads |
| --- | --- |
| Under a minute | Seconds, in steps of 5: `about 25 s` |
| Under an hour | Whole minutes: `about 3 min` |
| An hour or more | `about 1 h 5 min` |

The estimate follows the format, **Speed:**, the size, the frame rate and the range.

It's only an estimate. The figures behind it are the median of three measured exports per format at 1080p and 4K, of real 4K camera footage on an idle Apple M2 Max. On exports it wasn't fitted on, 30 seconds at 2560 × 1440, it came within 14 % of the real time. A slower Mac, a busy one or a heavy timeline takes longer.

## The footnote

The small line under the readout names what the file is made of. It lists these in order, leaving out whatever doesn't apply:

1. The codec, such as `H264`, `AV1` or `PRORES422`.
2. The container, unless it's the same word as the codec, as in `GIF`.
3. The AV1 speed, such as `Balanced`.
4. `24-bit` for a 24-bit WAV or AIFF.
5. The number of stems, such as `3 stems`.
6. The video rate, when you've picked a Quality tier. AV1 and VP9 rates read `usually ≤ …`, because the rate is a [soft cap](/export/av1-and-vp9/#the-rate-as-a-soft-cap).
7. The audio rate, when you've picked a Quality tier, such as `192 kbps audio`.
8. The loudness target, such as `−14 LUFS`.
9. `alpha`, when the format keeps transparency.

So a plain export reads `H264 · MP4`, an AV1 file `AV1 · MP4 · Balanced` or `AV1 · WEBM · Balanced`, and a transparent web movie `VP9 · WEBM · alpha`. With High quality and a loudness target at 1080p and 30 fps, an H.264 file reads `H264 · MP4 · 8.0 Mbps · 256 kbps audio · −14 LUFS`.

## The remembered choice

The sheet reopens on the last choices you exported with. Choosing **Export…** or **Add to Queue** records them, and **Cancel** doesn't. With nothing remembered, it opens on H.264 at the document's own size.

The remembered choice belongs to the app, not the project, so every document's sheet opens on it.

- Only what the format could use is remembered. After a WAV, for example, there's no size or frame rate to bring back.
- A remembered size row that the format doesn't list falls back to a row with the same numbers, or else to the format's default.
- A remembered **In/out range** falls back to **Whole project** on a document with no range.
- **Dynamic Range:** isn't remembered. It opens on **HDR (HLG)** every time.

To keep a set of choices under a name, save an [export preset](/export/presets/).

## Export or Add to Queue

The sheet ends in three buttons.

| Button | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| **Cancel** | Closes the sheet. Nothing is written and nothing is remembered. |
| **Export…** | Opens a save panel, then writes the file behind a [progress sheet](/export/progress-and-report/). It doesn't join the queue and never waits for memory. |
| **Add to Queue** | Opens the same save panel, then puts the job in the [Export Queue](/export/export-queue/). The job keeps the project as it is now, and you can go on editing. |

**Export…** and **Add to Queue** are greyed out while the sheet can't work out a valid file, for example with an empty custom field, or when the file would have no length.

The save panel suggests the project's name with the format's extension, such as `Board v1.2.mp4`. Its message says what's being written: "Export the timeline as a movie.", "Export the timeline as an animated GIF." or "Export the timeline's audio."

## Good to know

- An audio-only format on a timeline with no sound stops after the save panel with "There is nothing on the timeline to export — add a clip first."
- A custom size of a different shape from the canvas passes the readout, but the formats that keep transparency stop on it after the save panel. See [Transparent exports](/export/transparency/).

## With an agent

`export` starts the job and answers at once. Every agent export goes through the [Export Queue](/export/export-queue/), never behind a progress sheet. It takes the sheet's choices but not **Frame rate:**, so it writes the document's rate, or GIF's and APNG's own. It can also set a ceiling for the master limiter other than the sheet's fixed one, and it replaces an existing file at its path. See [Export: start, then poll](/mcp/export/).

## Related

- [Choose a format](/export/formats/)
- [Export presets](/export/presets/)
- [The Export Queue](/export/export-queue/)
- [What an export includes](/export/what-an-export-includes/)

Every export's sound goes through a master limiter, whatever you choose here. See [Export loudness](/export/loudness/).

## Unavailable controls

A control the chosen format can't use is greyed out rather than hidden, and its value isn't sent. So a greyed-out control never affects the file.

| Control | Available on |
| --- | --- |
| **Dynamic Range:** | HEVC 10-bit (MP4), AV1 (MP4), AV1 (WebM), VP9 (WebM), ProRes 422 (MOV) and ProRes 4444 (MOV). On any other format it's greyed out and shows **SDR version**, which is what that format writes. |
| **Speed:** | AV1 (MP4) and AV1 (WebM) |
| **Size:**, **Frame rate:** and **Burn in timecode** | Every format but the three audio-only ones |
| **Quality:** | Every format but ProRes, WAV, AIFF, GIF and APNG |
| **Bit depth:** | Audio only (WAV) and Audio only (AIFF) |
| **Stems:** | The three audio-only formats |
| **Loudness:** | Every format but GIF and APNG |

**Speed:**, **Bit depth:** and **Stems:** go on showing your last choice while they're greyed out, and it comes back when you pick a format that uses it.

**Range:** doesn't depend on the format. It's greyed out when the project has no in/out range. It's greyed out inside a nest too, even when the nest has a range, and its tooltip says why: an export writes the whole timeline, so it can't use a range that belongs to the nest. Leave the nest with <kbd>⌘↑</kbd> and set a range on the timeline.

## The readout line

The line under the controls says what size, rate and length the file will have. These are the file's real numbers, so a GIF's fitted size or an evened edge shows here.

| Kind of file | The readout looks like |
| --- | --- |
| A movie | `1920 × 1080 · 30 fps · 00:01:12:05` |
| An audio-only file | `Audio only · 00:01:12.200` |
| A GIF or APNG | The movie line, followed by `· 360 frames, no audio` |

When the sheet can't work out a valid file, the readout says what to fix and **Export…** and **Add to Queue** are greyed out. An empty custom field gives "Type a width and a height, or pick a size from the list." or "Type a loudness target in LUFS, or pick one from the list."

## Estimated time

On AV1 (MP4), AV1 (WebM), VP9 (WebM) and VP9 with Alpha (WebM) a second line estimates how long the export will take, for example `Estimated time: about 25 s`. The other formats show no estimate.

| How long | It reads |
| --- | --- |
| Under a minute | Seconds, in steps of 5: `about 25 s` |
| Under an hour | Whole minutes: `about 3 min` |
| An hour or more | `about 1 h 5 min` |

The estimate follows the format, **Speed:**, the size, the frame rate and the range.

It's only an estimate. The figures behind it are the median of three measured exports per format at 1080p and 4K, of real 4K camera footage on an idle Apple M2 Max. On exports it wasn't fitted on, 30 seconds at 2560 × 1440, it came within 14 % of the real time. A slower Mac, a busy one or a heavy timeline takes longer.

## The footnote

The small line under the readout names what the file is made of. It lists these in order, leaving out whatever doesn't apply:

1. The codec, such as `H264`, `AV1` or `PRORES422`.
2. The container, unless it's the same word as the codec, as in `GIF`.
3. The AV1 speed, such as `Balanced`.
4. `24-bit` for a 24-bit WAV or AIFF.
5. The number of stems, such as `3 stems`.
6. The video rate, when you've picked a Quality tier. AV1 and VP9 rates read `usually ≤ …`, because the rate is a [soft cap](/export/av1-and-vp9/#the-rate-as-a-soft-cap).
7. The audio rate, when you've picked a Quality tier, such as `192 kbps audio`.
8. The loudness target, such as `−14 LUFS`.
9. `alpha`, when the format keeps transparency.

So a plain export reads `H264 · MP4`, an AV1 file `AV1 · MP4 · Balanced` or `AV1 · WEBM · Balanced`, and a transparent web movie `VP9 · WEBM · alpha`. With High quality and a loudness target at 1080p and 30 fps, an H.264 file reads `H264 · MP4 · 8.0 Mbps · 256 kbps audio · −14 LUFS`.

## The remembered choice

The sheet reopens on the last choices you exported with. Choosing **Export…** or **Add to Queue** records them, and **Cancel** doesn't. With nothing remembered, it opens on H.264 at the document's own size.

The remembered choice belongs to the app, not the project, so every document's sheet opens on it.

- Only what the format could use is remembered. After a WAV, for example, there's no size or frame rate to bring back.
- A remembered size row that the format doesn't list falls back to a row with the same numbers, or else to the format's default.
- A remembered **In/out range** falls back to **Whole project** on a document with no range.
- **Dynamic Range:** isn't remembered. It opens on **HDR (HLG)** every time.

To keep a set of choices under a name, save an [export preset](/export/presets/).

## Export or Add to Queue

The sheet ends in three buttons.

| Button | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| **Cancel** | Closes the sheet. Nothing is written and nothing is remembered. |
| **Export…** | Opens a save panel, then writes the file behind a [progress sheet](/export/progress-and-report/). It doesn't join the queue and never waits for memory. |
| **Add to Queue** | Opens the same save panel, then puts the job in the [Export Queue](/export/export-queue/). The job keeps the project as it is now, and you can go on editing. |

**Export…** and **Add to Queue** are greyed out while the sheet can't work out a valid file, for example with an empty custom field, or when the file would have no length.

The save panel suggests the project's name with the format's extension, such as `Board v1.2.mp4`. Its message says what's being written: "Export the timeline as a movie.", "Export the timeline as an animated GIF." or "Export the timeline's audio."

## Good to know

- An audio-only format on a timeline with no sound stops after the save panel with "There is nothing on the timeline to export — add a clip first."
- A custom size of a different shape from the canvas passes the readout, but the formats that keep transparency stop on it after the save panel. See [Transparent exports](/export/transparency/).

## With an agent

`export` starts the job and answers at once. Every agent export goes through the [Export Queue](/export/export-queue/), never behind a progress sheet. It takes the sheet's choices but not **Frame rate:**, so it writes the document's rate, or GIF's and APNG's own. It can also set a ceiling for the master limiter other than the sheet's fixed one, and it replaces an existing file at its path. See [Export: start, then poll](/mcp/export/).

## Related

- [Choose a format](/export/formats/)
- [Export presets](/export/presets/)
- [The Export Queue](/export/export-queue/)
- [What an export includes](/export/what-an-export-includes/)
